1.why: All seven screens use a clean, static layout with no visible moving images or pop-ups.

2.why: Large headings, bold labels, colored notices, and prominent blue action buttons make important items stand out.

3.why: Each screen presents a clear heading and a prominent primary action, although the testing logs add some distracting content.

4.why: The user must complete and track several steps and remember a detailed password rule requiring length, letter cases, a number, and a symbol.

5.why: No password-manager option, explicit autofill control, or remember-me option is visible in any screenshot.

6.why: The identifier and recovery code appear prefilled on later screens, but no clearly labeled saved or familiar account items are shown.

7.why: Most instructions are brief and readable, though privacy, security, and testing text makes some screens longer than necessary.

8.why: No populated error message is shown, and the blank status areas do not demonstrate explanations of problems or corrective steps.

9.why: The recovery page supplies the exact mock identifier to enter, but the password screen gives rules without an example password.

10.why: The screenshots show only one recovery-code and password flow rather than clearly presented choices among password, code, face login, or other methods.

11.why: Each screen presents only one main action and at most one secondary action.

12.why: Status text clearly reports recovery preparation, privacy acceptance, and final appointment-request confirmation.

13.why: Short instructions and security tips accompany the identifier, code, password, privacy, and appointment steps.

14.why: Forms can be submitted again and the verification screen includes a visible Request another code action, although retry guidance is not shown for every step.

15.why: All screens consistently use the same header, card layout, typography, colors, notices, button styling, logs section, and footer.
